guard_streams.source: Closure of the May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
guard_streams.write_limit: The closure records a supplier-evidence collection and evaluation process. Existing and planned build submissions, future outputs and eligibility uses do not establish present-day selected-parcel orderability or measured speed.

facts.detail: The closure page was updated on 1 June 2026.
The May 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review concluded on 1 June 2026 at 5pm.
BDUK requested national broadband infrastructure coverage submissions from network providers.
The next National Rolling Open Market Review is due to launch in September 2026.
The process operates in January, May and September.
The review seeks current supplier build and planned build over the next three years.
The process supports strategic planning and prioritisation of procurement intervention areas.
Collected data informs GigaHubs and UK Gigabit Voucher eligibility.
Submissions are formally assessed for England and Wales.
Postcode- and UPRN-level outputs are to be published after evaluation is completed.

guard_streams.source: Closure of the January 2026 National Rolling Open Market Review
guard_streams.write_limit: NR OMR classifications are subsidy-control and procurement-planning evidence. They mix existing and planned supplier claims and cannot be treated as current selected-parcel coverage without exact current validation.

facts.detail: The January 2026 NR OMR ran from 6 January to 6 February 2026.
BDUK completed evaluation and issued formal responses to participating suppliers.
Premises were classified as Gigabit White, Grey, Black or Under Review.
White indicates no gigabit infrastructure and none likely within three years.
Grey indicates one qualifying current or planned gigabit infrastructure.
Black indicates two or more qualifying current or planned gigabit infrastructures.
Under Review covers unverified current claims or planned build with remaining delivery risk or evidence gaps.
BDUK states subsidy is provided only to premises designated White.
The England and Wales summary totals 31,054,557 premises across all four classifications.
UPRN-level outputs are provided in ten regional zip files and further split by Local Authority District.
